digest.component_or_area: llm model construction and provider fallback chains
propositions: A model class may reference an unreachable endpoint; today a single failure terminates the gate; users need per-class fallback chains to specify alternative models as fallback targets.
Fallback entries are inline model configs (same shape as primary slots) consumed into pydantic-ai's FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...) wrapper, not references to named presets.

The fallback_on predicate must be narrowed to errors where switching providers helps (availability/rate-limit classes) and must not mask credential or input-size failures; it is derived from failure.py's _RETRYABLE frozenset plus CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL to avoid drift.
Capabilities, cache settings, and tool guards are computed as the conservative intersection of all candidates before wrapping, so a chain withdraws a capability if any candidate lacks it.

Each fallback entry's endpoint is honored during model construction; the same provider path that builds the primary is used for each fallback, and all clients are registered on the same ProviderSession and closed exactly once.

Provenance records the ordered candidates and the ran_model from ModelResponse.model_name (not the synthetic FallbackModel.model_name string), so a verdict produced by a fallback does not misattest the primary.
